result.headline: Raising DQN's planning horizon from gamma 0.95 to 0.99 changed nothing measurable: the test mean is 21.4 ± 0.7 across three seeds (21.31 at 0.95), and 81% of seed 0's test games end by crashing into its own body.
result.summary:
**DQN (gamma 0.99, short vision, score reward, 10 min):** Seed 0 scored a test mean of 22.02 (median 21, best 35) over 100 fixed-seed games. Across the three seeds the test mean is 21.4 (range 20.67 to 22.02, std 0.68). The earlier gamma 0.95 baseline with the same vision and reward scored 21.31 on one seed, well inside that spread. Seed 0 took 195 steps per game and 9 steps per apple. Of its games, 81 ended in a body crash, 19 in a wall crash, and none starved.

The learning curve rose quickly and then flattened. The training mean of the last 100 games was 15.57 by minute 0.92 and stayed between 13 and 16.5 for the rest of the run, ending at 15.51. The best training game (41 apples) appeared by minute 4.6 and was never beaten. Because the mean only includes exploration moves, it reads lower than the greedy test score. Seed 0 logged 1.52M env steps, while seeds 1 and 2 logged about 2.45M each. The machine was shared by two runs, so that gap reflects load, not learning. Compare the algorithms by score per env step, not by wall-clock speed, and treat differences of about one point between single runs as noise.
result.diagnosis:
The most likely reason gamma did not help is that the short vision sees only the adjacent square. A longer planning horizon can only help if the agent can perceive the danger it is planning around. A snake that cannot see its body coming from several squares away will keep curling into itself, and valuing future crashes more does not give it the information to avoid them. The 81% body-crash share fits this. The plateau from minute 1 onward suggests the limit is what the agent observes, not how long it trains.

The lesson's own prediction was left blank in this run, so there is nothing to score. The other seeds (21.52, 20.67) and the lesson 03 baseline (21.31) support the view that the discount factor is not the bottleneck here.
result.learned: Planning further ahead only pays off when the agent can actually see the danger it is planning around. Before tuning how DQN values the future, check which crashes it makes and whether its inputs can reveal them.

recommendations.title: Give DQN rays vision instead of short
recommendations.why: If body crashes come from seeing only one square ahead, a vision that looks several squares along each direction should cut the 81% body-crash share and raise the test mean.
recommendations.change: Switch the vision from short to rays with depth 4, keeping gamma 0.99, score reward and 10 minutes.
recommendations.prediction: Test mean rises above 25 (from 21.4 across seeds), and the body-crash share falls below 70% of test games.
recommendations.question: Does seeing farther along each direction reduce body crashes more than planning further ahead did?

recommendations.title: Test a short horizon with gamma 0.8
recommendations.why: If planning horizon barely matters with this vision, a much shorter horizon should score about the same, which would confirm that gamma is not the bottleneck.
recommendations.change: Set DQN gamma to 0.8 (looks about 5 moves ahead), keeping everything else the same.
recommendations.prediction: Test mean stays within about 20 to 23, inside the seed spread of 20.67 to 22.02.
recommendations.question: Can DQN still learn to reach apples when it looks only about 5 moves ahead, and does that change the score?

recommendations.title: Train gamma 0.99 for 30 minutes
recommendations.why: The training mean flattened after about one minute. A longer run would show whether the plateau is a time limit or a limit of what the agent sees.
recommendations.change: Increase the time budget from 10 to 30 minutes, keeping gamma 0.99 and short vision.
recommendations.prediction: Training mean of the last 100 games stays between 13 and 17, and the test mean stays between 20 and 24.
recommendations.question: Is the plateau caused by too little training time, or by the short vision?
